where: The faint text tone: timestamps, hints, counts and the third step of the tone scale, on every surface and on a past calendar block
reason: At 7:1 the faint tone would be the same lightness as the muted tone, and the three steps that give a row its hierarchy (title, metadata, hint) would collapse into two.
route: Settings → Appearance → Contrast → High, or the system's increase-contrast setting with Contrast on Auto: every text tone then reaches at least 7:1.

where: The white label of a primary button and of the current item on the accent colour, for every accent theme
reason: 7:1 would need an accent a quarter darker than the brand's emerald (and every other accent the person can choose), which is the colour that makes OpenTodo recognisable.
route: The high-contrast presentation draws the button black on white or white on black, at better than 7:1.

where: Links, the current navigation item and accent icons drawn in the accent colour on the canvas, a card, a popover and a selected row

measured.light: 5.3:1 on the canvas with emerald, 5.0:1 with orange
measured.dark: 5.6:1 on a selected row with blue

reason: Accent text is the accent itself; a 7:1 version would be a different, darker colour next to the buttons, so links and the sidebar would no longer match the accent the person chose.
route: The high-contrast presentation draws links and the current item in the text colour with an underline or an outline.

where: Error, warning, success and information text in their status colours on the canvas, a card, a popover and a selected row (an overdue date, an error line, a completed check)

measured.light: 5.5:1 for an error on the canvas, 5.3:1 for success
measured.dark: 5.5:1 for an error on a popover

reason: The status colours carry meaning by their hue; at 7:1 they turn into four shades of near-black that read as text, not as a warning or a success.
route: The high-contrast presentation darkens or brightens every status colour to 7:1 while keeping its hue.

where: The muted tone on a selected row and on the tinted sidebar column
reason: The muted tone was retuned to 7:1 on every plain surface; reaching it on the accent tint too would push the tone to where it no longer differs from the default text.
route: The high-contrast presentation replaces the tint with an outline, so the muted tone sits on the plain surface at 7:1.

where: With a mouse or trackpad: sidebar rows, group headers and controls that sit side by side closer than 44 px, so a 44 px hit area would reach into the neighbour

measured.light: sidebar rows 36 px apart, group headers 24 px
measured.dark: sidebar rows 36 px apart, group headers 24 px

reason: Rows of 44 px with a fine pointer would make the sidebar and every group header a fifth taller, and the invisible hit area cannot grow into a neighbour that is itself a target.
route: On a touch screen every row and control is at least 44 px tall (the coarse-pointer rules); with a mouse the pointer is precise, and every control still has the invisible area wherever no neighbour claims it.

where: Paragraph spacing in a task's notes, a project's notes and comments
reason: A note in the task panel reads as one block of text; paragraphs 2 em apart would turn it into a document and push the fields below it off the screen.
route: The high-contrast presentation spaces the paragraphs of notes and comments 2 em apart, as the Help pages do by default.

where: Rows and their controls in the compact density
reason: Compact density is the person's choice to see more rows; a 44 px hit area for every control would overlap the rows above and below.
route: The comfortable density (the default) gives every control a hit area of at least 44 × 44 px, visible shape unchanged.
